btr.$note: 73 attachment(s) are listed for this Party's BTR1. 3 of 8 components are evidenced by an attachment name; the rest are unread, not missing. Adaptation and Article 6 are chapters inside the report rather than separate attachments, so no filename can evidence them and both stay unknown for every Party. Submission dates are not in this listing.

vulnerability.$note: From the 2026 bulk release, latest available year. ND-GAIN restates earlier years between releases (Cambodia 2021 read 40.1 in the edition cited by data/khm.json and 40.665 here); rank is not in the bulk file.

series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against.

country_profile.$note: Population is World Bank SP.POP.TOTL for the latest year published in the 2015–2025 window. Income group is the World Bank's own classification, not a UNFCCC one.

ndc_registry.$note: The registry states which submission is current and where it is. It carries no target figure, so nothing in ndc.* is derived from it.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: Kenya seeks to undertake an ambitious mitigation contribution towards the 2015 Agreement. Kenya therefore seeks to abate its GHG emissions by 30% by 2030 relative to the BAU scenario of 143 MtCO 2 eq; and in line with its sustainable development agenda. This is also subject to international support in the form of finance, investment, technology development and transfer, and capacity building. "Kenya's INDC includes both mitigation and adaptation components based on her national circumstances and in line with decisions 1/CP.19 and 1/CP.20. "
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 30% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to BAU scenario (143 MtCO2eq)
ndc_assessment.conditionality: Partially conditional (I)NDC (unspecified mix of domestic/international resources)
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy, Transportation, Industrial Processes, Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) and waste
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is Kenya's Second Nationally Determined Contribution 2031 - 2035, filed 2025-04-30. 51 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (5). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 99.5 MtCO₂e, DS-02 98.4 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 3 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 39.3 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 30% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to BAU scenario (143 MtCO2eq) It was classed partial. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +0.93°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.66°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
